purpose: Our documents cite other people's pages for facts we rely on: the CAVP black-box rule, the Kubernetes conformance mechanics, the DID Core test-suite count. Those quotations are load-bearing - the argument about what we borrow collapses if the source stops saying it - and nothing checked them until now. A citation that no longer resolves, or a page whose wording changed under a quote, is a silent defect in someone else's evidence.
rules: every entry: url, must_contain (at least one phrase), context (why we cite it), as_of
the page must fetch 2xx and every phrase must appear after whitespace normalisation, case-insensitively
phrases must be quotations, not summaries: if the phrase is our paraphrase, the check proves nothing
--cache lets an offline reader replay the same check; --no-network reports structure only and says UNVERIFIED

entries.claim: NIST's validation programme does not run the implementation under test; it supplies vectors and judges the returned outputs.
must_contain: Sends JSON formatted messaging and test data to the ACV client
entries.context: Why we separate 'setting the questions' from 'answering them' in the conformance proposal - the reference programme states that separation explicitly.

entries.claim: The certified Kubernetes programme is self-testing plus a submission reviewed by someone else, and certification is time-limited.
must_contain: There are over 90 Certified Kubernetes offerings
entries.context: Source for the three ingredients we lack: a manifest naming a legal entity, a reviewer who is not the author, and a listing that expires.

entries.claim: W3C recorded per-feature results across a large normative feature set rather than issuing a single badge.
entries.context: Why our coverage is published as a set of check ids and never as a percentage.
